questions.question: If a pre-trip inspection finds something unsafe, what should you do?

options.text: Continue driving and schedule a mechanic appointment after the trip.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Avoid using the unsafe parts but continue driving normally.

questions.explanation: You must fix any unsafe problems found during a pre-trip inspection. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: How can you avoid a hazard?

options.text: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder may be the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders can support the weight of a large vehicle.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim the extinguisher at the top of the flames.
Aim at the ground about two feet away from the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stay as far away from the flames as possible. Aim at the base of the fire, not the top.

questions.question: Is downshifting to a lower gear an effective way to slow a vehicle on a downhill slope?
questions.explanation: On steep hills, use engine braking as your main way to control speed. Downshift to a lower gear before you start driving downhill.

questions.question: When is it acceptable to fuel a bus while passengers are on board?

options.text: Only on trips longer than 100 miles.
Only if it cannot be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if it cannot be avoided.
questions.explanation: Do not fuel a bus with passengers on board unless absolutely necessary. Never fuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: When you apply the brakes, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle pulls to one side.
The vehicle does not pull to either side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle does not pull to either side.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side while braking, there may be a problem with the brakes.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load at the correct distance behind the driver's area.
Maintains safe distance from other vehicles.
Reduces the weight on the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. A broken suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: Is it illegal to drive a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.04 percent or higher?
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or more. You will lose your license if you drive a CMV while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Can you use road speed to decide when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: There are two ways to know when to upshift. First, watch the engine speed (rpm) and shift when you reach the top of the recommended range in your manual. Second, watch the speedometer (mph) and shift up as you reach the speeds each gear is designed for.

questions.question: When you start an engine, warning lights and buzzers should:
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away. These include lights for oil, coolant, charging systems, and the anti-lock braking system (ABS).

questions.question: Commercial vehicles must carry at least eight red reflective triangles.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles need three red reflective triangles, six fuses, or three liquid burning flares. They also need spare fuses and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:
questions.explanation: Follow posted speed limits in work zones. Slow down if weather is bad or workers are near the road.

questions.question: If you notice a safety issue or possible mechanical problem while driving, you should:

options.text: Wait to see if it fixes itself.
Write about it in your vehicle report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write about it in your vehicle report.
questions.explanation: At the end of your driving shift, you may need to write a report about your vehicle. Report anything that could cause safety problems or mechanical issues.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only needed when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Before driving, check that your vehicle has emergency equipment: spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or three liquid burning flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Your BAC is determined by how much alcohol you drank, how fast you drank it, and your body weight. Only time can lower your BAC as your body naturally processes the alcohol.

questions.question: Which of these is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or three liquid burning flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports your vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are extremely dangerous.

questions.question: When double clutching, if you stay in neutral too long and can't shift into the next gear, you should:

options.text: Stop the vehicle and start over.
Return to neutral, release the clutch, increase speed, and try again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to neutral, release the clutch, increase speed, and try again.
questions.explanation: If you can't shift into the next gear, don't force it. Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up the engine to match the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and might slow down traffic, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow).
